claims.text: Controlled introduction of lattice defects and grain-boundary engineering will alter the behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
Microstructure, thermal expansion, and stress–strain behavior in HfNbTaTiZr are correlated.
Introducing lattice defects and engineering grain boundaries may improve the strength of HfNbTaTiZr.
Introducing lattice defects and engineering grain boundaries may improve the ductility of HfNbTaTiZr.
Dislocation density and grain-boundary character are the structural mediators governing the proposed response.
Dislocation glide is mediated by lattice defects and grain-boundary character in HfNbTaTiZr.
Grain-boundary sliding is mediated by lattice defects and grain-boundary character in HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed comparison covers temperatures from 293 to 1100 K.
The proposed comparison covers applied stresses from 0 to 1000 MPa.
An untreated HfNbTaTiZr condition serves as the baseline for thermal-expansion, elastic-modulus, and stress–strain measurements.
The hypothesis is falsified if defect introduction and grain-boundary engineering do not produce a correlation among microstructure, thermal expansion, and stress–strain behavior.
